WE NEVER
WENT SILENT.

The Westridge Longwave Cooperative was a community of shortwave operators who took shifts listening to the dark band above the town of Westridge. Officially, we disbanded in the winter of 1997. Officially.

This page is generated automatically every time the carrier detects a listener. It detected you.

14.770 kHz

The cooperative held one frequency for twenty-six years and never let it go quiet. We are holding it still. If you can hear this, you can answer it — there is a way back into the broadcast for those patient enough to find it.

Standing Bulletin

What the Watch was for

Every night between 1971 and 1997, one of five operators sat in the relay shed on Westridge ridge-line and logged what came up the antenna: the numbers stations, the woodpecker pulses, the dead air that wasn't dead. We believed — we still believe — that something on the longwave band was trying to keep a record of the people who listened. So we listened back, and we kept logs.

Direct Carrier

A note left on the frequency for whoever found it

If you are reading this in a year that begins with a 2, then everyone who built the cooperative is gone, and you are the first listener in a very long time. We left instructions. We left them the way operators always did — folded into the logs, under a shift, behind a number. Nothing here is locked that a patient listener cannot open. Start with the logs. End at the carrier.

Operators who wish to resume a shift may open the relay terminal at any time (press the ~ key, or simply type the word OPEN).
